eli:is_member_of.label: is member of
eli:is_member_of.help: Indicates that this resource is conceptually included in another one. Typically the successive temporal versions of a given legislation are conceptually members of a single « abstract » resource.  For the notion of physical inclusion, eli:is_part_of is preferred

eli:realizes.label: realizes
eli:realizes.help: Relates a legal expression to the legal resource realised through that expression.

eli:embodies.label: embodies
eli:embodies.help: Relates a physical format to the legal expression embodied in that format.

eli:type_document.label: document type
eli:type_document.help: The type of a legal resource (e.g. "Directive", "Règlement grand ducal", "law", "règlement ministeriel", "draft proposition", "Parliamentary act", etc.).

eli:number.label: number
eli:number.help: An identifier or other disambiguating feature for a legal resource or legal expression. This can be the number of a legislation, the number of an article, or the issue number of an official journal.

eli:version.label: version
eli:version.help: A version status for the resource. Example of such values can be "Official Journal", "made", "consolidated", "proposed", "prospective", etc.

eli:version_date.label: date of version
eli:version_date.help: The point-in-time at which the provided description of the legislation is valid.

eli:date_publication.label: date of publication
eli:date_publication.help: Date of publication of the official version of the legislation, in hard copy or online, depending on what the official publication is, and when it was published.

eli:date_applicability.label: date of applicability
eli:date_applicability.help: The date at which the legislation becomes applicable. This is distinct from the date of entry into force : a text may come in force today, and state it will become applicable in 3 months.

eli:in_force.label: in force
eli:in_force.help: A value indicating the legal force of a legal resource or a legal expression. A set of values is defined by ELI. These values are: in force; partially in force; not in force

eli:first_date_entry_in_force.label: first date of entry into force
eli:first_date_entry_in_force.help: The first date any part of the legal resource or legal expression came into force (can be seen as the start date of a dc:valid range for this resource).

eli:date_no_longer_in_force.label: date of no longer in force
eli:date_no_longer_in_force.help: The last date any part of the legislation cease to be in force, if the date is known (can be seen as the end date of a dc:valid range for this resource).

eli:id_local.label: local identifier
eli:id_local.help: The unique identifier used in a local reference system to maintain backwards compatibility. For examples the CELEX at EU level, or the NOR in France.

eli:is_about.label: is about
eli:is_about.help: A subject for this legal resource.

eli:relevant_for.label: relevant for
eli:relevant_for.help: Refers to a place or an area associated with the resource. This covers the notions of jurisdiction, sovereignty, applicability or administrative area.

eli:juridiction.label: juridiction
eli:juridiction.help: The jurisdiction from which the legal resource originates.

eli:passed_by.label: passed by
eli:passed_by.help: The person or organization that originally passed or made the law : typically parliament (for primary legislation) or government (for secondary legislation). This indicates the "legal author" of the law, as opposed to its physical author. This property can be used multiple times to indicate both the agent that authored the text, and/or the agent that signed the text, thus turning it into an actual legislation. The relationship between current and any former law making body should be represented in the description of the agent itself.

eli:responsibility_of_agent.label: responsibility of (agent)
eli:responsibility_of_agent.help: An individual, organisation or organisational unit that has some kind of responsibility for the legislation. Typically the ministry who is/was in charge of elaborating the legislation, or the adressee for potential questions about the legislation once it is published. This property should be used when the value is selected from a vocabulary.

eli:responsibility_of.label: responsibility of
eli:responsibility_of.help: An individual, organisation or organisational unit that has some kind of responsibility for the legislation. Typically the ministry who is/was in charge of elaborating the legislation, or the adressee for potential questions about the legislation once it is published. This property should be used when the value is a free text.

eli:is_part_of.label: is part of
eli:is_part_of.help: A related resource in which the described resource is physically included. Covers the case of text included in an Official Journal, or an article included in a text. For the notion of conceptual/temporal inclusion, eli:is_member_of is preferred.

eli:has_part.label: has part
eli:has_part.help: A related resource that physically includes the described resource. Inverse of eli:is_part_of.

eli:has_member.label: has member
eli:has_member.help: Indicates that this resource conceptually includes another one. Inverse of eli:is_member_of.

eli:transposes.label: transposes
eli:transposes.help: Indicates that this legislation (or part of legislation) fulfills the objectives set by another legislation, by passing appropriate implementation measures. Typically, some legislations of European Union's member states or regions transpose European Directives. This indicates a legally binding link between the 2 legislations, at act or article level, from the original version of a national implementing measure to the legal resource Directive as published in the EU Official Journal. Can be used for transposition tables, once EU Publication Office has introduced ELI support down to the article level. Note that this should point to the legal resource of the Directive itself, not to one of its language-specific legal expression.

eli:applies.label: applies
eli:applies.help: Indicates that this legislation (or part of a legislation) somehow conforms with another legislation. This is an informative link, and it has no legal value. For legally-binding links of transposition, use the property transposes. This can be used for example: when a pre-existing law already conforms to a recent european directive (in that case it does not "transposes" it strictly speaking); when non-EU member states make sure their legislation is conformant with EU law without strictly speaking transposing it; when a legislation from a local authority conforms with a national legislation. Note that this should point to a LegalResource, not to a language-specific expression.

eli:consolidates.label: consolidates
eli:consolidates.help: Indicates that this consolidated legal resource or expression (which is usually the product of an editorial process that revises the legislation) takes into account another one. This property should be used multiple times to refer to both the original version or the previous consolidated version, and to the legislations making the change.

eli:based_on.label: based on
eli:based_on.help: Indicates that this legal resource is empowered by another one, typically a constitution, a treaty or an enabling act.

eli:changes.label: changes
eli:changes.help: Indicates that this legal resource or expression legally changes another. This encompasses the notions of amendment, replacement, repeal, or other types of change. This may be a direct change (textual or non-textual amendment) or a consequential or indirect change. Note, the property is to be used to express the existence of a change relationship between two acts rather than the existence of a consolidated version of the text that shows the result of the change. For consolidation relationships, use the "consolidates" property. The "commences", "repeals", "corrects" and "amends" properties specializes this property adding normalized semantics to the relationship.

eli:commences.label: commences
eli:commences.help: Indicates that this legal resource sets another legal resource into force. Note the date of entry into force of the other resource should be modified accordingly. Note also that it is not possible to indicate when the entry into force should happen.

eli:repeals.label: repeals
eli:repeals.help: Indicates that this legal resource or legal expression completely cancels, abrogates or replaces another. If a resource partially repeals another, this link can be used at the corresponding subdivision level being completely repealed.

eli:corrects.label: corrects
eli:corrects.help: Indicates that this resource introduces textual modifications (like correction of spelling mistakes) with no legal change in another resource, expression or format; typically corrigenda in EU legislation. For modifications that have a legal impact, use the "amends" property.

eli:amends.label: amends
eli:amends.help: Indicates that this resource introduces legal changes in another resource. For modifications that don’t have a legal impact, use the "corrects" property

eli:is_another_publication_of.label: is another publication of
eli:is_another_publication_of.help: Indicates that this resource is a new publication, in a different official journal, of another resource already published elsewhere, and cannot be considered to be the same resource (owl:sameAs cannot be used to avoid potential duplication of certain metadata, like the date of publication, or the publisher). Note that this is different from the exceptionnal cases of "republication", where the same resource is actually republished in the same official journal a few days after its initial publication, in case of errors.

eli:cites.label: cites
eli:cites.help: Citation in the text of the legislation. This includes verbatim citation and citations in referrals.

eli:related_to.label: related to
eli:related_to.help: Indicates a somehow related other document, not necessarily a legal resource. Note that citation links should use the cites property.

eli:title.label: title
eli:title.help: The title, or name, of an expression.

eli:title_short.label: short title
eli:title_short.help: Established short title of the expression (if any).

eli:title_alternative.label: alternative title
eli:title_alternative.help: An alternative title of the expression (if any).

eli:description.label: description
eli:description.help: An account of the resource (definition from Dubin Core), e.g a summary.

eli:format.label: format
eli:format.help: The file format, physical medium, or dimensions of the resource (definition from Dublin Core).

eli:is_exemplified_by.label: exemplified by (document)
eli:is_exemplified_by.help: Link to a concrete file URL.

eli:legal_value.label: legal value
eli:legal_value.help: The legal value associated with a specific format of a resource. A set of values is defined by ELI; these values are: "unofficial": no particular or special standing; "official": published by an organisation with the public task of making the information available (e.g. a consolidated version of a EU directive); "authoritative": the publisher gives some special status to the publication (e.g. "the Queens Printer" version of an Act of Parliament, or the OJ version of a EU Directive); "definitive": the text is conclusively what the law says, (e.g. the digitally signed version of an OJ).

eli:published_in_format.label: published in (URI)
eli:published_in_format.help: Reference to the Official Journal or other publication manifestation in which this format is published. This property should be used when the value is a suitable URI.

eli:published_in.label: published in
eli:published_in.help: Reference to the Official Journal or other publication manifestation in which this format is published. This property should be used when the value is a regular text.

eli:publisher_agent.label: publisher (agent)
eli:publisher_agent.help: An entity responsible for making the resource available (definition from Dublin Core). This property should be used when the value is selected from a vocabulary.

eli:publisher.label: publisher
eli:publisher.help: An entity responsible for making the resource available (definition from Dublin Core). This property should be used when the value is a free text.

eli:licence.label: license
eli:licence.help: A legal document giving official permission to do something with the resource (Definition from Dublin Core).

eli:rights.label: rights
eli:rights.help: Information about rights held in and over the resource (definition from Dublin Core). For example, that property can be used to provide a link to a page that describes the licensing terms.

eli:rightsholder_agent.label: rights holder (agent)
eli:rightsholder_agent.help: A person or organisation owning or managing rights over the resource (definition from Dublin Core). This property should be used when the value is selected from a vocabulary.

eli:rightsholder.label: rights holder
eli:rightsholder.help: A person or organisation owning or managing rights over the resource (definition from Dublin Core). This property should be used when the value is a free text.

elix:languages_list.label: languages list
elix:languages_list.help: List of all the languages used in the Legal expressions.

elix:formats_list.label: formats list
elix:formats_list.help: List of all the formats used in the Formats embodying a Legal expression.

elix:abstractLegalResourceUriScheme.label: URI scheme of Abstract legal resources
elix:abstractLegalResourceUriScheme.help: Define the pattern of the URI scheme. You can use variables such as {eli:type_document}, {eli:number}, etc.

elix:legalResourceUriScheme.label: URI scheme of the Legal resources
elix:legalResourceUriScheme.help: Define the pattern of the URI scheme. This URI scheme is the continuation of the URI scheme of the Abstract legal resources. You can use variables such as {eli:type_document}, {eli:number}, etc.

elix:legalExpressionUriScheme.label: URI scheme of the Legal expressions
elix:legalExpressionUriScheme.help: Define the pattern of the URI scheme. This URI scheme is the continuation of the URI scheme of the Legal resources. You can use variables such as {eli:type_document}, {eli:number}, {eli:language}, etc.

elix:formatUriScheme.label: URI scheme of the Formats
elix:formatUriScheme.help: Define the pattern of the URI scheme. This URI scheme is the continuation of the URI scheme of the Legal expressions. You can use variables such as {eli:type_document}, {eli:number}, {eli:language}, {eli:format}, etc.
